q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time Left Until Resolution
Today is 2026-08-15. Q2 FY2027 earnings would likely be released in August 2026 (since Q1 FY2027 ended April 26, 2026, and was reported May 20, 2026). This question appears to be asking about guidance already provided or about to be provided imminently. Resolution is essentially at hand or very recent.

## (b) Most Likely Outcome and Why

The research provides **explicit forward guidance from NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 earnings release (May 20, 2026)**: the company guided for Q2 FY2027 revenue of **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**.

This means NVIDIA's official guidance range is:
- **Lower bound: $89.18 billion** ($91.0B × 0.98)
- **Upper bound: $92.82 billion** ($91.0B × 1.02)

The company's guidance is the most direct answer to what "NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release" will be. The guidance was already issued on May 20, 2026.

Since the question asks what the guidance "will be," and we have the actual guidance from the official earnings release, the answer is the midpoint guidance of **$91.0 billion** with the stated ±2% range.

The research also notes:
- Analyst consensus is $91.8B (slightly above NVIDIA's midpoint)
- Analyst range: $90.3B to $96.7B
- Q1 FY2027 actual was $81.6B (20% QoQ growth)

## (c) What Would Push the Value Lower?

- Deteriorating demand signals between May and August 2026 (inventory corrections, weakening enterprise capex)
- Additional geopolitical restrictions on China sales (guidance already excludes China Data Center revenue)
- Unexpected competitive pressures from AMD or other AI chip manufacturers
- Macro recession concerns reducing customer capex commitments
- Supply chain disruptions

However, these would likely have been factored into guidance issued on May 20, 2026.

## (d) What Would Push the Value Higher?

- Stronger-than-expected demand from AI/data center buildout accelerating
- Better gross margins driving operating leverage
- Additional revenue from new product launches or higher ASPs
- China restrictions being lifted or relaxed
- Market share gains from competitors

The guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue as a conservative assumption.

## (e) Base Rate or Historical Reference Values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: **$81.6 billion** (ended April 26, 2026)
- Q2 FY2027 guided revenue: **$91.0 billion ±2%** (May 20, 2026 guidance)
- This represents ~11.4% QoQ growth implied by guidance
- Prior guidance accuracy: Q1 actual ($81.6B) was slightly below analyst average ($86.84B) but within typical guidance ranges

NVIDIA has historically provided conservative guidance that is often beaten, but this specific guidance of $91.0B ±2% is the binding forward guidance already issued.

## Interpretation

The question asks "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance" — this guidance was formally issued on May 20, 2026 at $91.0 billion ±2%. The actual Q2 FY2027 earnings release will either:
1. Reaffirm this guidance (if earnings are imminent on 2026-08-15)
2. Revise it up or down based on intervening business developments

Given that today is 2026-08-15 and Q2 earnings likely released in late August/early September (consistent with Q1 timing), we're essentially at the moment of earnings announcement or immediately after.

The most likely guidance value is the officially stated **$91.0 billion**, with the ±2% range capturing normal guidance bands.

The range given (99.5B to 115.5B) is quite wide and accommodates potential upward revisions if demand has accelerated significantly. However, barring major positive surprises, NVIDIA typically provides measured guidance.

NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion for Q1 FY227, ended April 26, 2026, marking an 85% increase year-over-year and a 20% increase from the previous quarter [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This surpassed the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's outlook, released on May 20, 2026, anticipates revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. The company explicitly states this outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). Analysts' consensus for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.8 billion, with estimates ranging from $90.3 billion to $96.7 billion [tickerleague.com](https://tickerleague.com/companies/NVDA/estimates). Expected GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are 74.9% and 75.0% respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. Operating expenses are projected at approximately $8.5 billion (GAAP) and $8.3 billion (non-GAAP) [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).
